name: Entero Healthcare Solutions Ltd
tagline: Pharma-distribution platform with a now six-quarter margin-expansion run (Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 5.0%, hit ahead of FY27 guidance), positive operating cash flow and ROE inflecting to ~20% — re-rated to ~61x earnings but still ~1x sales
business_overview: Entero Healthcare is a tech-enabled, pan-India pharmaceutical and healthcare-products distribution platform (Entero Direct, MedCords), founded 2018, connecting ~2,700+ manufacturers to ~95,000+ retail pharmacies and ~3,600 hospitals across ~500 districts via ~102+ warehouses. It grows both organically and via acquisition, distributing pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, medical devices, nutraceuticals, and private-label products.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 7,700-7,900 Cr (price ~Rs 1,750-1,810, late Aug 2026; roughly 1x TTM sales)
~10% ROCE (FY26); 3-yr avg ROE ~6%, but Q1 FY27 ROE annualised ~20.4% (9% -> 20.4% YoY)
Revenue Rs 1,940 Cr (+38.2% YoY; organic +17.8%, inorganic +20.4%); EBITDA margin 5.0% (+143 bps), EBITDA +94%; PAT Rs 52 Cr (+72%), owner PAT Rs 38 Cr (+37%)
Borrowings Rs 677 Cr (FY26, up from Rs 385 Cr) for acquisitions; interest coverage >18x; NWC days 61 (from 66); FY26 CFO +Rs 96 Cr (first positive year)
fundamentals_narrative: The deep read confirms the execution story and extends it. EBITDA margin has now expanded for six straight quarters — 2.8% -> 3.3% -> 3.6% -> 4.0% -> 4.5% (Q1-Q4 FY26) -> 5.0% (Q1 FY27) — hitting the full-year FY27 guidance a year early, with Q1 FY27 EBITDA up 94% YoY on 38.2% revenue growth. Operating cash flow turned positive for the first time in FY26 (+Rs 96 Cr after -Rs 37 Cr and -Rs 77 Cr in FY24/FY25), net working capital tightened to 61 days, and ROE inflected from 9% to ~20%. Two caveats the prior write-up understated: (1) borrowings rose to Rs 677 Cr in FY26 (from Rs 385 Cr) to fund a heavy M&A cadence — seven acquisitions in FY26, with Anand Chemiceutics alone slated to add Rs 1,000 Cr+ of FY27 revenue — though interest coverage stays comfortable at >18x; (2) PAT attributable to owners grew only 37% in Q1 FY27 versus the 72% headline, because acquired entities carry minority interests. The stock has also re-rated: at ~Rs 7,800 Cr it is now roughly 1x TTM sales and ~61x earnings, no longer 'below sales'. FY27 guidance: ~23% revenue growth, 5.0% EBITDA margin, and at least 50% of incremental EBITDA converting to operating cash.
technical_read: Stock has broken out well past the earlier Rs 1,468 high to ~Rs 1,750-1,810 in late Aug 2026 (52-week low Rs 944) — a strong uptrend that has priced the margin-expansion story to ~61x earnings and ~1x sales.
sentiment_summary: Newer thread (since June 2025) with substantive debate over valuation (EV/EBITDA ~22x on a 4% EBITDA-margin guide struck several posters as rich) versus the long growth-runway bull case (organized distribution is only ~10% of a ~Rs 2,70,000 Cr market, Entero itself only ~2-2.5% of total distribution). A detailed post (zygo23554, 28 loves) contextualized why Entero could sustain premium-to-global-peer multiples given India's fragmented, less-cyclical pharma distribution structure versus the four-player IT-distribution oligopoly comparison raised by a skeptic.

bse_notes: Reviewed to Aug 2026: Anand Chemiceutics acquisition (Q4 FY26, ~Rs 1,000 Cr+ FY27 revenue contribution) plus six other FY26 acquisitions; Fitch rating update Dec 2025; all seven AGM resolutions passed (Aug 2026); Q1 FY27 earnings call 10-Aug-2026. No pledge, no SEBI/regulatory action. bull_case: Six consecutive quarters of EBITDA margin expansion (2.8% -> 5.0%), with the 5.0% FY27 full-year guide already hit in Q1 FY27 — a confirmed, still-accelerating trend, EBITDA +94% YoY
Operating cash flow turned positive in FY26 (+Rs 96 Cr, first positive year) and NWC days tightened to 61 — the cash-conversion concern is now improving, not just promised
ROE inflected from 9% to ~20.4% YoY; organic revenue growth alone is ~18-20%, so growth is not purely acquisition-optical
Massive addressable market (organised distribution only ~10% of a ~Rs 2,70,000 Cr pharma-distribution market; Entero itself ~2-2.5% of total distribution) — long structural runway
Still only ~1x TTM sales for a top-3 player compounding revenue 38% YoY; ranvir (trusted) has tracked and implicitly endorsed the quarterly execution for over a year
bear_case: Inherently thin-margin distribution business — management's own ceiling is ~5-7% EBITDA margin, well below a typical multibagger margin profile
Acquisition-heavy model: seven acquisitions in FY26 pushed borrowings to Rs 677 Cr (from Rs 385 Cr); integration and roll-up execution risk is structural, not incidental
Owner economics lag the headline: Q1 FY27 PAT +72% but PAT attributable to owners only +37%, as acquired entities carry minority interests
Valuation has re-rated to ~61x earnings and ~1x sales — no longer the 'below TTM sales' bargain the original thesis leaned on
FII holding collapsed from ~23% to ~4% since the Feb-2024 IPO (partly offset by DIIs) — persistent selling by early institutional holders
verdict_headline: Six-quarter margin-expansion run now confirmed by primary filings, with cash flow and ROE inflecting — but the stock has re-rated to ~61x and the model leans hard on debt-funded M&A
verdict_reasoning: The deep read strengthens the thesis: margin expansion is now six quarters long and running ahead of the FY27 guide, FY26 operating cash flow turned positive, working capital tightened, and ROE moved from 9% to ~20%
The structural runway is intact (Entero at ~2-2.5% of a large, fragmenting distribution market) and organic growth is a healthy ~18-20%, so the story is not purely acquisition-optical

Tempering factors: borrowings nearly doubled to Rs 677 Cr on a seven-acquisition FY26, owner-attributable PAT grew only 37% vs the 72% headline, and the ~61x P/E / ~1x sales valuation is no longer cheap
Conviction set to Medium-High (down from a High reading in state.json): execution is genuinely confirmed, but thin absolute margins, M&A dependence and the re-rating cap it below High
No red flag; flagged for 30-day revisit
